summary: Bats test invocations inside node agent logs are routinely compacted to a TAP plan line plus a '+N more lines' pointer, with no per-test ok/not-ok lines retained inline. The largest verified instance in the preserved run directories is a 29-test mcp-proxy-policy.bats run whose compacted view shows only '1..29' and a truncation pointer; a second invocation of the same file is truncated identically. A single-file read elsewhere in the same node's log is truncated at '+73 more lines', which is the specific magnitude referenced when this class of truncation is discussed as 'the 73-line/73-test-scale run with no completed-test feedback'; the fixture below documents the verified 29-test case plus the exact 73-line truncation pointer since no single bats invocation with exactly 73 declared tests was found in the six preserved runs.

verifiedBatsTruncation.resultReference: compacted view pointer only; full output requires ralph_proxy_result_read

verified73LineTruncation.note: this is a file-read truncation, not a test-run truncation; included because it is the only exact '73' magnitude present in the preserved logs and matches the number referenced in the evidence request

operatorImpact: Whether truncating a test run or a file read, the compacted view hides individual completion lines behind a line-count pointer, so an operator or downstream agent cannot tell which specific tests passed or failed without an extra explicit full-output read step.
